requirements.title: Allocate-shape specs determine array bounds and zero extents
requirements.definition: When an ALLOCATE statement allocates an array using an allocate-shape-spec-list, the lower-bound and upper-bound expression values at execution determine the allocated array bounds. Later redefinition or undefinition of entities used in those expressions does not alter the bounds. An omitted lower bound is one, and an upper bound less than the lower bound gives that dimension extent zero and makes the array zero sized.

pending.explicit-lower-and-upper-bounds: PENDING complete source allocating an INTEGER allocatable vector with allocate-shape-spec 3:5, then observing LBOUND=3, UBOUND=5, SIZE=3, and literal element assignments [31,32,33]. The non-vacuous oracle is the inquiry tuple plus changed element literals after allocation; array declaration and ALLOCATE syntax remain 8.5.3 and 9.7.1.1 dependencies.
pending.default-lower-bound-one: PENDING complete source allocating INTEGER allocatable a(4) with the lower bound omitted, then observing LBOUND(a,1)=1, UBOUND(a,1)=4, SIZE(a)=4, and a literal assignment to a(4). The default is material because a companion explicit 0:3 allocation would have the same extent but different lower bound.
pending.bounds-captured-after-expression-change: PENDING complete source with scalar bound variables lo=2 and hi=4 used in ALLOCATE(a(lo:hi)), then reassigning lo and hi to different literals before observing LBOUND=2 and UBOUND=4. The oracle is the original bound tuple and a reached sentinel, not storage layout or compiler agreement.
pending.zero-extent-single-dimension: PENDING complete source allocating a(5:3), observing SIZE(a)=0, LBOUND/UBOUND values only through permitted inquiry semantics for a zero-sized allocation, and avoiding any element reference. The oracle is zero size and successful STAT=0, not reading unallocated or nonexistent elements.
pending.zero-sized-array-defined-status-boundary: PENDING source plan that allocates a zero-sized INTEGER array without SOURCE= and then uses only SIZE and STAT plus a separately assigned sentinel to show the program path. Definition-status consequences are checked only through 19.6.5(18) ownership, with no attempt to read an element.

requirements.title: Upper-bounds expressions determine rank-wide allocation bounds
requirements.definition: When an ALLOCATE statement uses the parenthesized upper-bounds-expr allocation form for an array, the upper bounds are determined from that expression, lower bounds are determined by lower-bounds-expr if present or otherwise by one, scalar lower or upper bound expressions are broadcast to the shape of the other expression, and any upper element below its corresponding lower element gives zero extent in that dimension and zero size for the array. Later changes to entities in the bounds expressions do not alter the bounds.

pending.vector-upper-bounds-default-lowers: PENDING complete source allocating a rank-two INTEGER array with the upper-bounds-expr vector [2,3] and no lower-bounds-expr, then observing LBOUND=[1,1], UBOUND=[2,3], SHAPE=[2,3], and a literal assigned to a(2,3). The vector form is material because no allocate-shape-spec-list appears.
pending.vector-lower-and-upper-bounds: PENDING complete source allocating with lower-bounds-expr [0,4] and upper-bounds-expr [1,6], then observing LBOUND=[0,4], UBOUND=[1,6], SHAPE=[2,3], and a literal stored at a(1,6). The oracle uses inquiry results and a defined element only.
pending.scalar-lower-broadcast: PENDING complete source using scalar lower-bounds-expr 0 and vector upper-bounds-expr [1,2] for a rank-two allocation, observing LBOUND=[0,0] and SHAPE=[2,3]. A repair/control with vector lower [0,0] should produce the same literal observations without treating compiler agreement as the oracle.
pending.scalar-upper-broadcast: PENDING complete source using vector lower-bounds-expr [2,3] and scalar upper-bounds-expr 4, observing LBOUND=[2,3], UBOUND=[4,4], SHAPE=[3,2], and assigned corner literals. The scalar broadcast is non-vacuous because the two lower bounds differ.
pending.zero-extent-from-one-dimension: PENDING complete source allocating rank-two bounds lower [1,5], upper [3,4], then observing SIZE=0 and SHAPE with one zero extent while never referencing elements. STAT=0 and a reached sentinel distinguish a successful zero-size allocation from an allocation error.

requirements.title: Coarray allocation expressions determine cobounds
requirements.definition: For an ALLOCATE statement executed for a coarray, the lower and upper cobound expression values determine the allocated cobounds. Later redefinition or undefinition of entities in those expressions does not alter the cobounds, and an omitted lower cobound has the default value one.

pending.explicit-cobounds: PENDING multi-image source allocating an allocatable coarray x[2:*] on all active images in the current team, then observing LCOBOUND=2 and the permitted upper cobound for the final codimension with STAT=0. The oracle is coarray inquiry results under a separately gated multi-image profile, not remote payload reads.
pending.default-lower-cobound-one: PENDING multi-image source allocating x[*] or an equivalent final codimension with omitted lower cobound, observing LCOBOUND=1 and successful STAT=0 on every active image. The lower-cobound default is material because a separate explicit lower-cobound control uses a different literal lower value.
pending.cobounds-captured-after-expression-chang: PENDING multi-image source with cobound variables initialized to fixed literals before ALLOCATE and then redefined after successful allocation. The oracle is the original LCOBOUND/UCOBOUND inquiry tuple plus STAT=0; no observation depends on address arithmetic or communication beyond required synchronization.
pending.multi-image-cobound-inquiries: PENDING source plan requiring at least two images to allocate the same coarray and compare local inquiry results to fixed expected literals on each active image. Multi-image execution is a separately gated capability; absence of that profile leaves this facet pending.

requirements.title: Coarray upper cobounds shall not be less than lower cobounds
requirements.definition: For each explicit allocate-coshape-spec used in coarray allocation, the upper cobound shall not be less than the lower cobound. This is a prose execution restriction on cobound values, distinct from the R940/R941 syntax and C945/C946 coarray-spec ownership in 9.7.1.1.

pending.reversed-cobound-rejected-or-error: PENDING multi-image diagnostic/control source: attempt to allocate an otherwise valid allocatable coarray with an explicit nonfinal cobound such as [5:3,*], and repair only the upper cobound to satisfy upper>=lower. The repaired control observes STAT=0 and fixed cobound inquiries; the invalidity is attributable to S9.7.1.2-004, not to R940/R941 syntax, C945 coarray-spec presence, or C946 corank count.

requirements.title: Coarray allocation must be corresponding across active images of the current team
requirements.definition: If an allocation specifies a coarray, its dynamic type, corresponding type parameter values, bounds, and cobounds shall be the same on every active image in the current team. Additional correspondence requirements apply to coarray dummy arguments, ultimate components of dummy arguments, ultimate components of array elements, and unsaved local coarrays of recursive procedures, including same ultimate arguments, same declaration name and scoping unit where specified, same array element position, and same recursion depth where specified.

pending.same-type-params-bounds-cobounds: PENDING multi-image positive-control source where all active images allocate the same allocatable coarray with identical dynamic type, length parameter, bounds, and cobounds, then observe identical local inquiry tuples and STAT=0. Multi-image execution is separately gated; the plan does not claim processors must detect mismatches.
pending.dummy-ultimate-corresponding-coarrays: PENDING multi-image source with a procedure taking an allocatable coarray dummy and every active image passing corresponding coarray actual arguments, then observing fixed cobound inquiry literals after allocation. The positive control satisfies the requirement rather than using noncorresponding actuals that could be invalid under argument association rules.
pending.dummy-component-same-name-and-scope: PENDING multi-image source with a derived-type dummy whose ultimate coarray component is declared with the same component name in the same scoping unit on all active images. The oracle is a literal component value assigned after successful allocation plus identical inquiry results; type definition ownership remains 7.5 dependencies.
pending.recursive-dummy-component-same-depth: PENDING multi-image source entering a recursive procedure to the same literal depth on all active images before allocating an ultimate coarray component of a dummy argument. The oracle is the depth sentinel and STAT=0 on every image; uneven-depth negatives are attributed to S9.7.1.2-005 only if all declaration and argument requirements remain otherwise satisfied.
pending.array-element-component-same-position: PENDING multi-image source allocating a coarray component of the same array element position on every active image, with distinct element-position sentinel values proving the selected element is material. The control avoids array-bounds or component-designator violations owned by 9.4.2 and 9.5.3.3.
pending.unsaved-local-recursive-same-depth: PENDING multi-image source allocating an unsaved local coarray in a recursive procedure at the same literal recursion depth on all active images and observing STAT=0 plus a depth sentinel. This requires multi-image and recursion support as separate gates.
pending.mismatch-attribution-boundary: PENDING multi-image source/diagnostic-policy plan requiring at least two images for a deliberately mismatched coarray allocation across active images, with a repaired version changing only the mismatched bound, type parameter, element position, or recursion depth. Multi-image execution is a separately gated capability. The catalogue records that violations are attributable to S9.7.1.2-005 and that the note says processors are not required to detect at least the same-bounds violation or deadlocks.

requirements.title: Coarray allocation synchronizes active images and allocates only on all-image success
requirements.definition: Execution of an ALLOCATE statement for which an allocate-object is a coarray includes implicit synchronization of all active images in the current team. A stopped or failed image in the current team causes an error condition. If no other error occurs, each active image is delayed after the statement until all other active images in the team have executed the same statement the same number of times in the team. Segments before the ALLOCATE on one active image precede segments after it on another, and the coarray shall not become allocated on an image unless it is successfully allocated on all active images in the team.

pending.implicit-synchronization: PENDING multi-image source in which one image writes a pre-allocation sentinel to a coarray-visible state before all images execute the same ALLOCATE, and another image observes a post-allocation local sentinel only after the statement. The oracle is ordered literal sentinels under a gated multi-image profile, not timing or deadlock detection.
pending.same-statement-same-count-delay: PENDING multi-image source where all active images execute the same coarray ALLOCATE twice with a per-iteration literal counter recorded after each statement. The oracle is the ordered counters and STAT=0 on every image; a mismatched-count source is a separate non-executed diagnostic-policy plan.
pending.segment-ordering: PENDING multi-image source using defined scalar literals before and after coarray allocation to demonstrate the segment precedence promised by p5 through a standard synchronization-compatible observation. The plan must avoid races and must be reviewed with 11.7.2 ownership before fixture approval.
pending.stopped-or-failed-image-error-condition: PENDING source plan for an environment that can provide a stopped or failed image in the current team, expecting the ALLOCATE with STAT= to report an error condition according to 9.7.4. This is separately gated and is not a deliberate resource-allocation failure oracle.
pending.all-image-success-before-allocated: PENDING multi-image source allocating a coarray with STAT= and then checking ALLOCATED locally on every active image only when all STAT values are zero. The non-vacuous oracle is the all-image vector of STAT=0 and ALLOCATED=.TRUE.; cases with a stopped/failed image stay gated and pending.

requirements.title: Pointer and allocatable source expressions must have usable status
requirements.definition: If the ALLOCATE statement source-expr is a pointer, it shall be associated with a target. If source-expr is allocatable, it shall be allocated. This status requirement applies to the source-expr used by SOURCE= or MOLD= and is separate from the R930/R932 spelling and C950/C951 type, kind, and rank constraints.

pending.associated-pointer-source: PENDING source/control pair using SOURCE= with an INTEGER pointer source associated with a defined TARGET literal 74, allocating an INTEGER allocatable object and observing value 74 plus STAT=0. A non-executed invalid variant nullifies only that pointer before ALLOCATE; the intended violation is S9.7.1.2-007, with review noting possible overlap with general pointer-reference rules in 8.5.14/9.2.
pending.allocated-allocatable-source: PENDING source/control pair using an allocated INTEGER allocatable source assigned literal 75 for SOURCE=, observing the allocated destination value and ALLOCATED=.TRUE. A non-executed invalid variant deallocates only the source before ALLOCATE; the intended violation is S9.7.1.2-007 rather than C950 rank/type compatibility or 9.7.1.1 allocation syntax.

requirements.title: SOURCE-shaped allocation inherits shape and lower bounds from source-expr
requirements.definition: When an ALLOCATE statement allocates an array without an allocate-shape-spec-list or upper-bounds-expr, the array is allocated with the shape of source-expr and each lower bound equal to the corresponding element of LBOUND(source-expr). Later changes to the source-expr bounds do not alter the allocated array bounds.

pending.shape-from-source-expr: PENDING complete source with an allocated source array s(-2:0,4:5) and ALLOCATE(a,SOURCE=s) without explicit bounds, observing SHAPE(a)=[3,2], copied literals, and STAT=0. The source shape is material because no allocate-shape-spec-list or upper-bounds-expr appears.
pending.lower-bounds-from-source-lbound: PENDING complete source using SOURCE= from an array whose lower bounds are [-2,4], then observing LBOUND(a)=[-2,4] and corner literal values. The plan avoids assuming storage order beyond standard array element references.
pending.source-bound-changes-do-not-affect: PENDING source using a pointer or allocatable source whose bounds are changed by reassociation or reallocation after ALLOCATE, then observing that the already allocated object retains the original LBOUND/UBOUND tuple and copied literals. The later source change is made through defined operations only.

requirements.definition: If SOURCE= appears, source-expr shall be conformable with the allocation. This prose conformance requirement is separate from the 9.7.1.1 C950 rank alternatives and from the array bound forms that establish the allocation shape.

pending.source-conformable-with-allocation: PENDING diagnostic/control source: allocate a rank-one allocatable array with explicit bounds of extent three and SOURCE= an array expression of extent two, then repair only the allocation extent or source extent so they conform and observe copied literals [1,2,3]. The invalidity is attributed to S9.7.1.2-009 after confirming R929-R941 syntax, C943 array-shape presence, and C950 rank compatibility are otherwise satisfied.

requirements.title: SOURCE= allocation uses the provided value and evaluates source once
requirements.definition: For SOURCE= allocation, if an allocate-object is not polymorphic and source-expr is polymorphic with a dynamic type different from its declared type, the value provided for that allocate-object is the ancestor component of source-expr that has the allocate-object type; otherwise the value provided is source-expr. On successful allocation, an allocate-object with the same rank as source-expr becomes that provided value, while if the ranks differ each element becomes the provided value. The source-expr is evaluated exactly once for each ALLOCATE statement execution.

pending.nonpolymorphic-ancestor-component-value: PENDING complete source with a polymorphic source whose dynamic type extends a parent type and a nonpolymorphic parent allocate-object. SOURCE= should allocate the parent object with the ancestor component value, observed through parent component literals. The source avoids relying on extension components being present in the nonpolymorphic destination.
pending.ordinary-source-value-same-rank: PENDING complete source allocating an INTEGER rank-one array with SOURCE=[11,22,33], observing destination values [11,22,33], SHAPE=[3], and STAT=0. The literal vector provides the independent oracle and the same-rank path is material.
pending.scalar-source-broadcast-to-array: PENDING complete source allocating an INTEGER array with explicit shape and scalar SOURCE=7, observing every element equals 7 and a changed shape inquiry. The oracle is literal value replication plus SIZE>1, not storage inspection.
pending.array-source-to-same-rank-array: PENDING complete source allocating a rank-two array from a rank-two source with distinct corner literals, observing the full set of copied literals and bounds established by p7 or explicit shape. The plan first establishes the source is defined.
pending.source-expression-evaluated-once: PENDING complete source where SOURCE= is a function that increments a saved counter and returns a fixed literal or array. After one ALLOCATE execution the oracle is counter=1 and the allocated value literal; the function has no side effects that alter allocation conformance.
pending.definition-status-from-source-boundary: PENDING source plan pairing a defined SOURCE= component and an undefined SOURCE= component only through 19.6.5(20)/19.6.6(13) ownership. Any future executable fixture may observe only the defined copied literal and must not read a subobject whose corresponding source subobject is undefined.

requirements.title: Length type parameter mismatches are ALLOCATE error conditions
requirements.definition: An ALLOCATE statement has an error condition if a length type parameter value specified by type-spec differs from the corresponding nondeferred type parameter in any allocate-object declaration. It also has an error condition if a nondeferred length type parameter value of an allocate-object differs from the corresponding type parameter of source-expr.

pending.type-spec-nondeferred-length-mismatch-er: PENDING diagnostic/runtime source using a CHARACTER or parameterized derived-type allocate-object with a nondeferred length parameter and a type-spec specifying a different length, with STAT= present. The oracle is a nonzero STAT or the 9.7.4-defined error indication; the repaired control changes only the type-spec length and observes STAT=0 and expected length inquiry. This is not a deliberate resource exhaustion test.
pending.source-nondeferred-length-mismatch-error: PENDING diagnostic/runtime source using SOURCE= or MOLD= with a source length parameter different from a nondeferred length parameter of the allocate-object, all other type/kind/rank constraints satisfied, and STAT= present. The repaired control changes only the source length and observes STAT=0 plus a literal length inquiry; invalidity is attributable to S9.7.1.2-012.

Numbered syntax rules and constraints carry the 4.2 detection/reporting duty; unnumbered prose effects, execution-time status checks, STAT values, image participation, processor-dependent conditions, and coarray synchronization requirements are not promoted to mandatory static diagnostics. Multi-image execution, failed/stopped-image handling, and teams are separately gated capabilities in this suite.

requirements.title: ALLOCATE error conditions are processor dependent and no-STAT errors terminate
requirements.definition: The set of ALLOCATE statement error conditions is processor dependent. If an error condition occurs during execution of an ALLOCATE statement that lacks a STAT= specifier, error termination is initiated. STAT= and ERRMSG= details are owned by 9.7.4 and 9.7.5.

pending.processor-dependent-error-set-boundary: PENDING source-only classification plan listing only standard-specified error conditions from 9.7.1.2 p5, p10, p11 and 9.7.1.3 p1 as portable facets, while leaving resource exhaustion or processor-specific allocation limits untested. The oracle for future cases must be a standard STAT/ERRMSG or termination rule, not deliberately causing allocation failure.
pending.error-without-stat-initiates-error-termi: PENDING non-resource error source, such as allocating an already allocated allocatable variable without STAT=, in an otherwise conforming minimal program. The oracle is the standard error-termination path defined by 9.7.1.2 p11 and the repaired control adds STAT= or deallocates first to reach a literal sentinel; attribution must exclude syntax and type incompatibility errors.

requirements.oracle: All facets are pending source plans. Positive plans use independent literal values, allocation/association inquiry results, bounds/shape inquiry results, STAT/ERRMSG observations where allowed by the cited owner, or reached-control-flow sentinels that first establish the preconditions for the operation. Negative plans use an otherwise conforming source and a minimal repair, with the violation attributed to the named requirement rather than to ALLOCATE syntax, attribute ownership, designator formation, undefined data, unsupported launch mode, allocation-resource failure, emitted code, addresses, TRANSFER, or compiler agreement.
